vulnerability.title: Enable the File Access Policy Service
vulnerability.description: The File Access Policy service should be enabled. The fapolicyd service can be enabled with the following command: $ sudo systemctl enable fapolicyd.service
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then SYSTEMCTL_EXEC='/usr/bin/systemctl' "$SYSTEMCTL_EXEC" unmask 'fapolicyd.service' if [[ $("$SYSTEMCTL_EXEC" is-system-running) != "offline" ]]; then "$SYSTEMCTL_EXEC" start 'fapolicyd.service' fi "$SYSTEMCTL_EXEC" enable 'fapolicyd.service' else >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done' fi

triage_decision.reason: Enabling the fapolicyd service is a standard service enablement that does not affect authentication, networking, or filesystem integrity. It follows typical STIG hardening patterns and is unlikely to cause lockout or system breakage.

The plan correctly enables the fapolicyd.service, which addresses the vulnerability. The sequence of systemctl commands will make the service active immediately and start on boot. While a check for the system’s online state would make it a bit more robust, the current plan will functionally resolve the issue.
concerns: Does not check whether the system is in an offline state before attempting to start the service; may result in an error if the service cannot be started in that situation.
No error handling on systemctl commands could result in silent failures if permissions or other conditions prevent execution.
Unmasking will produce an error if the service is not masked, but this is harmless.
suggested_improvements: Add a guard to skip starting the service when systemctl is-system-running == "offline".
Use systemctl status fapolicyd.service to verify the service is actually running before enabling.
Redirect or capture errors, e.g., "systemctl unmask fapolicyd.service || true" to avoid aborting the script if already unmasked.
Consider enabling with "systemctl enable --now fapolicyd.service" to combine enable and start in one step, reducing the number of commands.
